speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; I see you are a neonate presenting three days after birth with seizures and lethargy. To begin my evaluation, were you delivered via Cesarean section, and if so, was there any delay in the delivery of the placenta?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) with seizures. The history of chorioamnionitis, low Apgar scores (3 and 6), and a 1100g infant at 31 weeks presenting with seizures and lethargy is highly suggestive of perinatal asphyxia. I will now request an EEG and MRI brain images to assess for encephalopathy and seizure focus.
